environment.description: Same Spring Boot application deployed inside a bubblewrap (bwrap) sandbox invoked with --unshare-all --new-session, bind-mounted into a minimal chroot at /srv/app containing only the JRE runtime jars, application jar, and /tmp (noexec,nosuid). The process runs under a dedicated UID (65534/nobody) with PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS. The chroot contains no /proc, no /sys, no /etc/passwd, no /etc/shadow, no device nodes. Network namespace is shared but outbound connections are restricted via nftables to only the database host (10.0.2.15:5432) and the health check responder (127.0.0.1:8080). The AWS metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254 and ECS credential endpoint 169.254.170.2 are explicitly blocked in the nftables OUTPUT chain. Additionally, a seccomp profile (allowlist mode) permits only: read, write, openat (restricted via RESOLVE_BENEATH to /srv/app), close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, brk, futex, clone3, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, socket (AF_INET only), connect, accept, sendto, recvfrom, getpid, exit_group, sigaltstack, rt_sigaction. Notably, execve/execveat are NOT in the allowlist, meaning Runtime.exec() and ProcessBuilder calls will receive SIGSYS.
